## Proof

Let
$$I = \int_0^1 \left(x - \tfrac{1}{2}\right) F(x)(1 - F(x))\,dx.$$

Apply the change of variables $x \mapsto 1-x$:
$$I = \int_0^1 \left(1-x - \tfrac{1}{2}\right) F(1-x)\bigl(1 - F(1-x)\bigr)\,dx = \int_0^1 \left(\tfrac{1}{2} - x\right) F(1-x)\bigl(1 - F(1-x)\bigr)\,dx.$$

By the symmetry hypothesis $F(1-x) = 1 - F(x)$, hence
$$1 - F(1-x) = F(x),$$
and therefore
$$F(1-x)\bigl(1 - F(1-x)\bigr) = (1 - F(x))\,F(x) = F(x)(1 - F(x)).$$

Substituting back,
$$I = \int_0^1 \left(\tfrac{1}{2} - x\right) F(x)(1 - F(x))\,dx = -\int_0^1 \left(x - \tfrac{1}{2}\right) F(x)(1 - F(x))\,dx = -I.$$

Thus $I = -I$, which gives $2I = 0$, so
$$I = 0.$$

The identity is **proved**.

### PROOF COMPLETE
